checked_scope: The Pareto criterion for finite unpopularity factor, maximum aggregation across components, and the common-order formula.
checks: A positive challenger win count with zero loss count is exactly a Pareto improvement; finiteness iff Pareto optimal. A Pareto-improved incumbent weakly reduces every challenger win count and increases its loss count, so factor cannot increase after max with 1.

For disjoint components, r_i<=U s_i even when s_i=0 if all factors finite; summing yields global factor<=max component, attained by changing one component. Independent component minimizers give the same maximum for optimal factors; additive amplification for margins does not transfer.

Common-order Pareto optima fill the first min(n,h) houses. With 0<h<n the shift chain gives h winners/one loser, and h>=n gives n-1 winners/one loser. Counting winners plus a necessary loser matches max(1,min(h,n-1)); n<=1 or h=0 separately has factor1.
